grammar_focus: 介词固定搭配(take interest in / on display / suspended from / attached to / familiar to / in response to / emit from),外加“辅音字母+y → -ies、元音字母+y → -s”的名词复数与动词第三人称单数拼写规则(baby→babies、try→tries、donkey→donkeys、pay→pays)(原创承载 NCE3 L18 考点·无需净化·参观一场会动、带电的现代雕塑展)
scene: 如今现代雕塑几乎不再让人吃惊了。“现代艺术只能在博物馆里看”这种说法是错的。就连对艺术毫无兴趣的人,也不可能没注意到公园里、商店外那些造型古怪的现代雕塑;有些所谓“现代”的作品,已经在公共场所立了将近八十年,我们早就见怪不怪。即便如此,最近市中心的一场雕塑展还是让我吃了一惊。走进美术馆,我看到的第一样东西是墙上贴着的告示:“请勿触摸展品,有些很危险!”展出的都是会动的雕塑。造型古怪、从天花板上垂下、随一阵风摆动的东西,大家早就熟悉。可这些展品不一样:靠着一面墙,排着一根根细长金属丝,末端连着金属球。球被磁化过,整天互相吸引、又互相排斥。大厅正中立着几座高大的结构,里面装满彩灯,像发了疯的交通信号灯一样不停闪烁。小黑盒子里迸出火花,红灯气呼呼地忽明忽暗。整个展厅活像一场史前电子设备展。这些稀奇古怪的造型,似乎不光要在情感上震撼你,还要真的电你一下!

grammar_card.title: 介词固定搭配 + -y 变 -ies/-s 拼写
grammar_card.intro: ①很多短语的介词是固定的,要整体记:take (an) interest in（对…感兴趣）、on display（展出中）、suspended from（从…垂下）、attached to（连在…上）、familiar to sb（为某人所熟悉）、in response to（响应…）、emit … from（从…发出）。②名词变复数、动词变第三人称单数时,以 -y 结尾要看前一个字母:辅音字母 + y → 去 y 加 -ies（baby→babies、city→cities、try→tries）;元音字母 + y → 直接加 -s（donkey→donkeys、day→days、pay→pays）。

rows: no interest in art / attached to the wall
on display / suspended from the ceiling
familiar to everybody / in response to the wind

specialRules.rule: 固定搭配的介词不能随意换:be attached to（✓ 连在…上）不用 attached on;familiar to sb（为某人所熟悉)别和 familiar with sth（熟悉某事)混。
辅音字母 + y → 去 y 加 -ies:city→cities、try→tries;元音字母(a/e/o/u) + y → 直接加 -s:day→days、pay→pays。
美语拼写:colored(英式 coloured);“店铺”store(英式 shop)、“市中心”downtown(英式 city centre)。本课已按美语写。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — How might some of the exhibits have been dangerous?
options: They could give visitors an electric shock
They could fall from the ceiling
They were made of broken glass

passage: These days modern sculpture hardly surprises anyone. The idea that modern art can only be seen in museums is mistaken. Even people who take no interest in art cannot help noticing strange shapes on display in the parks and squares of many cities. We have all gotten used to them; some so-called 'modern' pieces have stood in public for nearly eighty years. Even so, I was surprised by a recent exhibition downtown. The first thing I saw when I walked into the gallery was a notice attached to the wall: 'Do not touch the exhibits. Some of them are dangerous!' The objects on display were pieces of moving sculpture. Oddly shaped forms suspended from the ceiling, which sway in response to a gust of wind, are familiar to everybody. These exhibits, however, were different. Lined up along one wall were long thin wires attached to metal spheres. The spheres had been magnetized, so they attracted or repelled one another all day long. In the center of the hall stood tall structures full of colored lights that flickered like traffic signals gone mad. Sparks were emitted from little black boxes, and red lamps flashed on and off angrily. The whole room felt like a display of prehistoric electronic gadgets. These peculiar forms seemed designed not only to shock people emotionally, but to give them a real electric shock as well!

stage5.stem: "A notice was attached ___ the wall near the door."(attach 后接哪个介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 门边墙上贴着一张告示。

stage5.stem_cn: 这些造型随一阵风摆动。

stage5.stem: "Such swinging shapes are familiar ___ everybody."(familiar 后接哪个介词)
stage5.stem_cn: 这种摆动的造型人人都熟悉。
